events.description: Three men, three eras and one hidden connection shape this boldly cinematic Spanish drama about love, secrets and the weight of the past. Shifting between 1932, 1937 and 2017 with ease, at first these three stories seem completely separate, but gradually connections emerge between the men at their centre. Desire, buried family truths and a forgotten piece of history bind their lives across generations, with an unfinished work of Federico García Lorca hanging over the whole story. From its virtuoso opening scene, this sweeping epic announces itself as an assured piece of filmmaking. Stunning location work, breathtaking composition and meticulous period detail create a richly textured world where personal and national histories collide. Look out for supporting turns from Glenn Close and a heavily award-tipped Penélope Cruz.

events.description: A spire pierces the Edinburgh sky, blackened by centuries of secrets and storms. The city below shudders with history both whispered and shouted. Uncover a side of Edinburgh most never see on this self-guided audio tour. Move from the looming Scott Monument to the timeworn stones of Greyfriars Kirk, through the halls of New College and beyond, chasing the tales that haunt every step. Why did a silent midnight duel near the kirk change the fate of a nation? Which monument conceals the scars of a forgotten rebellion? What odd ritual once echoed through New College’s secluded courtyards? Wander ancient closes and grand crescents. Trace the city’s shadows and scandals in corners tourists rush past. Every moment here tilts between awe and revelation, promising fresh eyes on a living legend. Take the first step into Edinburgh’s tangled heart and let its true story unfold.

Rhys Ifans and Laura Linney star as two people brought together by humour, dance and Parkinson’s in a life-affirming British dramedy about finding reasons to keep moving. Tony and Emma are diagnosed with Parkinson’s on the same day and continue to drift in and out of each other’s lives over the next five years. What begins as an unlikely friendship slowly becomes something deeper, as they discover that living with Parkinson’s doesn’t mean giving up on fun, romance or trying something new. Directed by John Madden (Shakespeare in Love, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel) and written by Paul Mayhew-Archer, whose own experience of Parkinson’s gives the film a rare personal insight, Onwards and Sideways has genuine warmth behind its humour. Rhys Ifans and Laura Linney make an appealing pair in a film that looks at Parkinson’s without letting the illness dominate the story. Sometimes you just have to keep moving - even if it’s sideways.

events.description: Daria is one of the most actively growing names in the techno scene. She has played some of the world’s most renowned institutions, with frequent bookings at Berghain, Bassiani, Fabric, London’s Fold and festivals like Tomorrowland, Junction 2, Awakenings, Time Warp and played at Amnesia, Hi and DC10 in her first Ibiza season. As a DJ, Daria never aims to deliver what is expected of her, but rather tries to convey her personal narratives through music. Daria views music as the most genuine method of communication, empathy and unity - a tool that helps her transform her distinctive energy into a story that can be shared with people on the dance floor. She desires to not only provide a danceable and enjoyable set but inspire and introduce people to something fresh and daring. Daria’s style is rooted in hard and groovy techno, often infused with elements of breakbeat, electro, hardcore, or jungle, making her performances rich in variety and unpredictability.

Britains chief meteorological officer James Stagg (Andrew Scott) is called upon to deliver the most consequential forecast in history, locking him into a tense standoff with the entire Allied leadership. The wrong conditions could devastate the largest ever seaborne invasion, while any delay risks German intelligence catching on. We are pleased to present a major solo show by Aberdeen-based printmaker Ade Adesina (b.1980. Nigeria), bringing together an expansive collection of the artist’s monumental woodcuts, etchings, linocuts and screen-prints. Exploring urgent global themes, including climate change and colonial histories, Adesina draws from the past and present, to imagine possible futures. His works carefully balance beauty with a darker underbelly, revealing the impact of human intervention on the natural world. Informed by his African roots, combined with the influence of British culture and global travels, Adesina’s practice is steeped in the traditions of Fine Art printmaking. On first glance his work appears as classical landscapes or still lifes, however they invite and reward closer looking, as complex narratives and entangled iconography is revealed. The exhibition will contain a newly commissioned print produced specially for Edinburgh.

Gidiki are at the forefront of the folk revival scene in Greece. Their songs 'Αφούσης' and 'Το Γλέντι' were viral hits in 2024 and 2025. Laurie Corlett-Donald is a solo artist based in Edinburgh who makes contemporary classical music blended with electronic ambient undertones. He started his career playing in bands when he was nineteen including Discopolis and Stillhound, touring extensively and releasing three records he turned his hand to solo music production, initially releasing club music under the moniker Trembler until he shifted towards more ambient sonics and string arrangements. After many years of learning and experimenting the project turned into ‘Dunedin’ - a multimedia exploration of his hometown. Drawing on experiences of wanting to be away from Edinburgh, going out and seeing new places and yet inevitably ending up back there, the record acts as a homage to a city that is entrenched in the soul of who he is. Collaborating with local writers, short stories were made for each of the tracks that he made and the namesake comes from the stories, not the other way around. The only brief being - ‘your connection to Edinburgh’. For the live show he is going ‘off grid’ as much as possible, blending analog modular, piano and synths with Justyna Jablonksa on cello, Emma Lloyd on violin and Luisa Brown on fiddle and electronics to reimagine the album for a live environment.

Born in Rio de Janeiro, four-times Grammy nominee, singer, composer, arranger, and instrumentalist Joyce Moreno has in her portfolio over 400 recordings of songs she has authored, interpreted by the greatest names in Brazilian popular music: from Elis Regina and Gal Costa to Milton Nascimento, Sergio Mendes, and countless others. Beyond Brazil, Joyce’s work has been recorded by Annie Lennox, Wallace Roney, Omara Portuondo, Black Eyed Peas, David Sanchez, Jon Lucien, Claus Ogerman, Gerry Mulligan, Till Brönner, Flora Purim, to name a few. Joyce’s compositions have been featured in film soundtracks (e.g., The Player by Robert Altman and Legally Blonde by Robert Luketic), animations (the Japanese anime Wolf’s Rain, in partnership with composer Yoko Kanno), TV programs, and theatrical productions. In the early 1990s, her music was embraced by DJs all over the world, starting from London, and her tune 'Aldeia de Ogum' became a massive worldwide dancefloor hit, with numerous remixes. Since the beginning of her career, Joyce’s registered trademark has been the first-person feminine voice, which she pioneered; she was the first Brazilian female songwriter to express herself in this form, opening the way for countless other artists who followed. Joyce Moreno has received four nominations for the Latin Grammy (2000, 2004, 2005, 2010), and numerous awards, worldwide and in her native Brazil.

The 5-star critically acclaimed Tony Award nominated and Olivier Award-winning play starring John Lithgow (Killers of the Flower Moon, The Crown) as Roald Dahl, GIANT comes to the big screen. With a stellar cast including Aya Cash, Elliot Levey and Rachael Stirling, the play was filmed live in London’s West End ahead of its sold-out Broadway run. A world-famous children’s author under threat. A battle of wills in the wake of scandal. And one chance to make amends. It's the summer of 1983, The Witches is about to hit the shelves and Roald Dahl is making last-minute edits. But the outcry at his recent, explicitly antisemitic article wont die down. Across a single afternoon at his family home, and rocked by an unexpectedly explosive confrontation, Dahl is forced to choose: make a public apology or risk his name and reputation. Inspired by real events, GIANT explores with dark humour the difference between considered opinion and dangerous rhetoric offering a complicated portrait of a fiendishly charismatic icon.

ai.en: The Delines perform at Traverse Theatre on a UK and EU tour in support of their sixth album.

events.description: Doors 7.30pm, 8pmstart The Delines return to tour the UK and EU in support of their 6th album out March 2024. The album was just mastered and bring more of their country-soul and their first to be recorded in the UK produced by John Parish (PJ Harvey). Edinburgh will be their only Scottish (and UK show North of Manchester) for all of 2027. Their debut record, COLFAX, appeared in 2014 and surprised fans and critics alike. Evoking a beat-up Dusty Springfield or a weary Rickie Lee Jones, COLFAX made over a dozen top ten year end lists. It was a four-year wait until their sophomore effort, THE IMPERIAL was released, a record that spent two weeks on top of the UK official Americana charts with the band playing sold out shows across the UK and Europe. The band returned with their cinematic third album THE SEA DRIFT which Americana UK and BBC6 Gideon Coe both made their ‘Album of the Year’. Penned by guitarist and songwriter Willy Vlautin with arrangements by keyboardist Cory Gray and the rhythm section of Sean Oldham and Freddy Trujillo. It was followed by Mr Luck & Ms Doom in 2025 and The Set Up in 2026 which had many journalists calling it their best yet. Vlautin is no stranger to critical acclaim, enjoying cult success and rave reviews from the likes of the New York Times, Washington Post, Uncut, Rolling Stone and Mojo, both as a novelist with eight books under his belt (two of his books have become major films). Willy, Oldham and Trujillo also lead the alt-country outfit…

ai.en: The Specials Ltd. perform the Gangsters Tour 2027 at La Belle Angèle, a tribute to the 2-Tone band The Specials.

events.description: The Specials Ltd.'Gangsters' Tour 2027 The Specials Ltd. are the world's most authentic and original tribute to 2-Tone Records Legends, The Specials. When the original line up of The Specials split in 1981 they left behind a legacy which has been unrivaled by a single band since. The Specials formed their own 2-Tone record label which launched the recording careers of Madness, The Beat, The Bodysnatchers and The Selecter. The Specials Ltd are an 8 piece group who recreate the passion and enthusiasm of The Specials, bringing back memories of those who were there first time around and showing younger fans what they missed. The Specials Ltd perform classics and fan favourites such as Gangsters, Do The Dog, Message To You Rudy, Stereotype, Rat Race, Do Nothing, Monkey Man, Too Much Too Young and more. An AGMP Concerts presentation.

title.en: The Hooten Hallers with support from Toby Mottershead

events.description: For the past nineteen years, The Hooten Hallers have been tearing up the road, blending blues, garage rock, country, punk, and jazz into a sound that's truly their own. The band's high-octane live shows must be experienced to be believed, with their raucous jams, tight vocal harmonies, and danceable grooves that make for a wild night and an unforgettable music experience.​ This powerhouse trio is driven by the vocal growl and swirling electric and lap steel guitars of John Randall, the powerful drumming and falsetto howl of Andy Rehm, and the burning baritone and bass saxophone lines of Kellie Everett. It’s Morphine meets ZZ Top mixed with a dash of George Thorogood and Tom Waits. But anyone who has seen this band live knows that this group is unlike anything they’ve experienced before. When The Hooten Hallers come to town, you know it’s gonna be a party! Toby Mottershead Toby is one of the best Edinburgh-based blues exponents and will need no introducing to his many supporters.

ai.en: RUTS DC present 50 years of The Ruts, celebrating their music from 1977 to 2027, at The Crossing with special guests.

events.description: RUTS DC present 50 years of RUTS Music (1977-2027) THE RUTS + special guests In 1977, The Ruts emerged from London with a sound unlike anybody else around them - the raw urgency of punk colliding with reggae, dub and rock, driven by formidable musicianship and a fierce sense of purpose. With Malcolm Owen, Paul Fox, Dave Ruffy and Segs Jennings, The Ruts created a body of music whose power has endured far beyond its original moment. After losing Malcolm Owen in 1980, the remaining members chose integrity over nostalgia by re-inventing themselves as Ruts DC, eventually losing Paul Fox in 2007. Ruts DC remain a living, evolving band to this day. But the time has come to celebrate the whole story. This tour is about taking the music that exploded out of a movement and bringing it onto a stage in 2027 with all its urgency and relevance intact. Music made across five decades - from the albums The Crack and Grin & Bear It, through Animal Now, Rhythm Collision, Music Must Destroy, and Counterculture? with the classic singles In A Rut. Babylon's Burning. Something That I Said. Jah War. Staring At The Rude Boys. West One (Shine On Me) and more. An AGMP Concerts presentation. This event is for over 18s only - No refunds will be issued for under 18s

ai.en: Too Bad Jims perform at La Belle Angèle, with support from Jed Potts & The Hillman Hunters. The band takes its name from an album by RL Burnside.

events.description: The Too Bad Jims got their name from the seminal Fat Possum album "Too Bad Jim" by the hugely influential blues musician RL Burnside. The band plays a gritty high-octane mix of North Mississippi Hill Country blues and boogie. It all initially started as a casual collaboration between two veteran and multiple award-winning musicians, Little Victor and Son Jack Jr. and they shortly after rounded out the trio with the one and only Nick Simonon (Brother of Paul Simonon of The Clash) on drums and things really started cookin’! Their unique and unusual combination of dual rough and ready vocals, bare-bones electric guitars, slashing bottleneck, and a heavily rhythm-oriented groove, delivers a hypnotic, raw, and earthy sound typical of a North Mississippi juke joint. After relocating to the London area from Seattle, Washington USA, Son Jack Jr (an avid long-time player of this style of blues) got in touch with Little Victor Mac whom he had befriended on social media since Victor's glory days with Louisiana Red in the late 2000s The two men never met in person until a couple of years ago but ever since their first jam, they sounded like they’d been playing together since day one. Little Victor (who moved to England a little before Son Jack Jr.) has deep knowledge of this style of music, particularly RL Burnside.
